source.title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures Associated with the Invariant Subspace Problem

accepted.question_text: For which bounded operators T on a separable real or complex Banach space X does there exist a non-trivial closed T-invariant subspace M, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} and M not equal to X such that T(M) is contained in M?

Let X be an infinite-dimensional separable real Banach space and let T:X -> X be a continuous operator with no non-trivial closed invariant subspaces. Let X_c be the complexification X + iX, and let T_c:X_c -> X_c be the complex-linear extension defined by T_c(x + iy) = T x + i T y. What can be determined about the closed invariant subspaces of T_c?

Does every positive operator on a separable Banach lattice have a non-trivial closed invariant subspace, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} and M not equal to the whole Banach lattice such that the operator maps M into M?

Does every adjoint operator have a non-trivial closed invariant subspace, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} and M not equal to the whole space such that the adjoint operator maps M into M?

Let X be an infinite-dimensional separable real Banach space and let T:X -> X be a continuous operator with no non-trivial closed invariant subspaces. Let X_c be the complexification of X and let T_c:X_c -> X_c be the natural complex-linear extension T_c(x + iy) = T x + i T y. Is it true that T_c also has no non-trivial closed invariant subspaces?

Let X be an infinite-dimensional separable real Banach space and let T:X -> X be a continuous operator with no non-trivial closed invariant subspaces. Let T_c be the natural complex-linear extension of T to the complexification X_c. Does T_c have a minimal non-zero closed invariant subspace V, meaning a non-zero closed T_c-invariant subspace such that every closed T_c-invariant subspace U contained in V is either {0} or V itself?

Let A be a subalgebra of L(X), the algebra of bounded operators on an infinite-dimensional separable Banach space X. Say that A is n-transitive if, for every linearly independent n-tuple (x_1,...,x_n) in X^n, the orbit of that tuple under the diagonal algebra A^(n) is dense in X^n. If A is n-transitive for some integer n > 1, must A be (n+1)-transitive?

Let X be a real Banach space and let A be a strictly transitive algebra of bounded operators on X, meaning that for every two non-zero vectors x and y in X there is an operator A_0 in the algebra with A_0 x = y. Must A be dense in L(X) in the weak operator topology?
accepted.context_brief: Strict transitivity over real Banach spaces

accepted.question_text: Let T be a bounded operator on a real or complex Banach space with no non-trivial closed invariant subspaces. Let Alg T denote the algebra of all polynomials in T, let the bar denote closure in the weak operator topology, and let {T}' denote the commutant of T, the algebra of all bounded operators that commute with T. Is the weak-operator-topology closure of Alg T equal to {T}'?

Let A be a transitive algebra of bounded operators on a real or complex Banach space X, meaning that A has no common non-trivial closed invariant subspaces. Suppose A has the Closure Property: every linear operator S:Y -> X, defined on a linear subspace Y of X and commuting with every operator in A, is closable. Must A be dense in L(X) in the weak operator topology?

Can a commutative algebra A of bounded operators on a real or complex Banach space be transitive while also having the Closure Property? Equivalently, is it true that every commutative operator algebra with the Closure Property has a common non-trivial closed invariant subspace?
